items.t: Said a tax relief proposal is the largest bipartisan legislative tax relief proposal in over a generation and would ease financial burdens on families, seniors and renters.
items.q: It is the largest bipartisan legislative tax relief proposal in over a generation," Spilka said. "This tax relief bill will help alleviate many, many financial burdens that our families, our seniors, our renters face and put real dollars in their pockets.

items.t: Said the state needs to make child care and early education more affordable and accessible.
items.q: We need to make child care and early education more affordable and accessible.

items.t: Said a bill would help increase salaries, create career ladders for early educators and stabilize early education programs.
items.q: The bill would help increase salaries and create career ladders so early educators can make their jobs a long-term career, while also stabilizing early education programs, Spilka said.

items.t: Said that even one child going to school hungry is too many, in announcing Senate passage of Senate Bill No. 298.
items.q: announced Senate Bill No. 298’s passage in a tweet, stating that “even one child going to school hungry is too many.”

items.t: Said she was an early and ardent supporter of equal marriage and transgender protections.
items.q: She was an early and ardent supporter of equal marriage and transgender protections.

items.t: Advocated for paid family leave, pay equity, maternal health and abortion access.
items.q: Spilka has worked to elevate women’s leadership through mentorship programs, public exhibits, and advocacy for issues such as paid family leave, pay equity, maternal health, and reproductive freedom.

record.t: Became President of the Massachusetts Senate in 2018.
record.q: Since 2005, she has represented Framingham, Ashland, and surrounding communities in the Senate and has paired broad statewide leadership with a strong commitment to strengthening MetroWest since becoming President in 2018.

record.t: Spearheaded the creation of the MetroWest Regional Transit Authority.
record.q: Spearheaded the creation of the MetroWest Regional Transit Authority, increasing mobility for employees, seniors and the disabled in MetroWest

record.t: Led passage of the Student Opportunity Act, which expanded support for public schools.
record.q: Spilka led passage of the landmark Student Opportunity Act, which expanded support for public schools and nearly doubled funding for Framingham.

record.t: Created MassEducate, which provides statewide tuition-free community college.
record.q: She also created MassEducate, which provides statewide tuition‑free community college.

record.t: Secured $12 million to clean the contaminated General Chemical site near Harmony Grove Elementary School.
record.q: secured $12 million to clean the contaminated General Chemical site near Harmony Grove Elementary School.
